explanations: luna: The source section reads the root و-س-ط spatially as the place between two sides; this ayah calls the community an أمة وسطا and immediately makes it a witness-community over humanity. Its distinct ethical sense links centrality to the section's other root ش-ه-د, while remaining different from the horses' position in a crowd. | terra: أُمَّةً وَسَطًا ... شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ unites both roots developed by the section: being in the middle and bearing witness over humanity.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع opens a local human crowd toward the final gathering; this ayah says that wherever people are, God will bring them all together (جميعا). It makes the assembly universal across places. | terra: Wherever people may be, يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا promises their convergence from every location into a single divine summons.
terra: وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ turns the audience from numbered pilgrimage days toward the final gathering to God.

luna: The source section's root و-س-ط marks the center between the edges of a crowd; this ayah marks the middle prayer (الصلاة الوسطى) within the prayer sequence. The link is specifically central position, though here it orders prayers rather than people in space. | terra: الصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَى uses the section's middle-root for a prayer situated or valued as the middle, a non-martial application of between-ness.
terra: Whether people disclose or conceal what is within themselves, God calls them to account for it, closely matching the collected contents of breasts.

luna: The source section says the root ج-م-ع names the final gathering; the prayer here calls God جامع الناس for a day about which there is no doubt. It gives the crowd's gathering a universal and certain horizon. | terra: The prayer addresses رَبَّنَا as جَامِعُ النَّاسِ for an unquestionable day, matching the section's movement from their Lord to all humanity gathered.
terra: The disbelievers are told they will be overcome and تُحْشَرُونَ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ, giving the assembled movement a defeated destination.

luna: The source section describes horses penetrating the middle of a human crowd; this ayah names the two hosts who met at Badr (التقى الجمعان), one fighting for God and one disbelieving. It gives the battle-crowd image a direct Qur'anic counterpart.

luna: The source section opens جَمْعًا from a battle crowd toward the final day; this ayah asks what it will be like when people are gathered for a doubtless day and each soul is repaid in full. The verse makes the assembly a setting for reckoning. | terra: فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ describes an unquestionable day when every soul is paid fully, giving purpose to the section's universal collection.
terra: Whether people تُخْفُوا مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ or reveal it, God knows it, directly anticipating the day's collection of breast-secrets.

luna: The source section says what is in the breasts is collected on the day; this ayah says each soul will find the good and evil it did present before it. It gives a concrete disclosure of each person's record. | terra: On the day each soul finds its good and evil مُحْضَرًا, inward moral contents become present objects from which it cannot distance itself.
terra: The command to hold fast all together and not divide makes human gathering an ethical unity explicitly bounded by dispersal.
terra: God tests مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ and purifies what is in hearts, a process parallel to making their inner contents distinct and manifest.

luna: The source section pictures a crowd caught by a raid; this ayah recalls the day the two groups met (التقى الجمعان) and says some turned away. It supplies the reversal of a crowd's cohesion under pressure. | terra: The people who turned back on the day the two hosts met locate moral failure inside the same battlefield meeting of gathered crowds.
terra: Whether people die or are killed, لَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُحْشَرُونَ relocates every scattered death into one eventual destination.

luna: The source section's crowd is a human group caught in battle; this ayah refers to the day the two groups met and says what befell them was by God's permission. It frames a battle crowd's fate as more than its visible force. | terra: What struck the believers on the day the two hosts met occurred by God's permission, another exact battlefield use of the gathered-crowd formula.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع names the mass of people under attack; here believers are warned that people have gathered against them (جمعوا لكم). It depicts a crowd as a threat assembling before an encounter. | terra: النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ presents a human force gathered against the believers; here the crowd is the approaching threat rather than the surprised target.

luna: The source section's witness-root ش-ه-د describes being present; this ayah asks what it will be like when a witness is brought from every community and the Messenger is a witness over his people. It turns the gathered communities into witnesses and the witnessed. | terra: A witness is brought مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ and the Messenger is brought as witness over these people, populating the universal assembly with its witnesses.
terra: The community is told to mobilize in separate groups or all together, a military contrast between smaller companies and one massed force.

luna: The source section connects the human جمع to the Day of Gathering; this ayah says God will surely gather people for the Day of Resurrection. Its direct root wording confirms that the crowd-word reaches the final assembly. | terra: God promises لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ and grounds it in His uniquely truthful speech, a direct formulation of the great gathering.

luna: The source section moves from a crowded human group to the day of gathering; this ayah says God will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (جامع المنافقين والكافرين). It gives the assembly a specifically punitive destination.

luna: The source section explains the root ش-ه-د through witnessing and being present; this ayah says Jesus will be a witness over the People of the Book on Resurrection Day. It places a witness over a community in the final accounting. | terra: Jesus will be a witness against the People of the Book on Resurrection, assigning a named witness to a particular community in the assembly.

luna: The source section's root و-س-ط means the place between two ends; this ayah uses أوسط for the ordinary, moderate measure of food fed to one's family. The relation is a measured middle rather than a crowd's spatial center, so it is a secondary lexical connection. | terra: مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ uses the middle-root for the household's median or fair food, showing the root's evaluative extension from spatial middle.
terra: The hunting rule ends with fear of the God إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, making final assembly the horizon of conduct during earthly gathering and travel.
terra: يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ depicts a particular assembly within the universal day and immediately questions its witnesses about their reception.
terra: Jesus says he was شَهِيدًا only مَا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ; his witness depended on presence among the people, while God's witness continues after his departure.

luna: The source section contrasts a small attacked people with the gathering of all humanity; this ayah says God will surely assemble people for the Resurrection Day, with no doubt in it. It makes the final assembly the scale beyond any tribe. | terra: لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ follows the statement that mercy is written upon God, placing universal gathering under that lordly relation.

luna: The source section turns an attacked crowd into humanity gathered before God; here God gathers everyone and asks the idolaters where their claimed partners are. The assembled crowd faces the collapse of its former affiliations. | terra: وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا stages everyone together before God, who then addresses the associators inside that assembled scene.
terra: Birds and earth-creatures are communities like humans and إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ يُحْشَرُونَ, widening the boundary of creaturely gathering beyond the human crowd.
terra: The warning addresses those who fear أَنْ يُحْشَرُوا إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ without protector or intercessor, emphasizing exposed presence before their Lord.
terra: The command to pray and fear God closes with وَهُوَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, directing the audience toward its common assembly.
terra: The trumpet-day belongs to the knower of the unseen and the witnessed, joining resurrection's summons to the boundary between hidden and manifest.

luna: The source section pictures everyone collected on the final day; this ayah says people come to God individually (فرادى), stripped of what they had been given. It marks that universal assembly does not erase each person's solitary accounting.

luna: The source section scales a human crowd up to a universal gathering; this ayah gathers jinn and humans together and has the jinn acknowledge the people who followed them. It broadens the assembly and exposes the relation between its two groups. | terra: وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا gathers jinn and humans together, making the section's all-human scale still wider and exposing their relations.
terra: In the assembled address to jinn and humans, شَهِدْنَا عَلَى أَنْفُسِنَا makes the gathered beings testify against themselves about meeting this day.
terra: Divine force reaches a settlement by night or during its midday rest, a nonlexical parallel to a community being caught by a sudden incursion.
terra: Successive communities enter the Fire until all have joined one another there, making a final collected company whose members curse each other.
terra: Pharaoh's counselors tell him to send gatherers through the cities, a direct human mechanism for producing the public crowd of magicians.

luna: The source section's root ش-ه-د names being present and bearing witness; this ayah has the descendants of Adam testify to God's lordship (شهدنا). It offers a collective witness-scene that contrasts with the final gathering: humanity's testimony begins before its worldly life. | terra: Human descendants are brought forth and made to أَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ, an earlier collective scene of self-testimony before the final gathering.
terra: The call to respond to God and the Messenger concludes وَأَنَّهُ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, making gathering to Him the audience's final summons.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع names a human battle crowd; this ayah calls the day the two groups met (التقى الجمعان) the Day of Decision. It joins the battlefield meeting of crowds to a decisive day. | terra: يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ makes a battle encounter of two gathered hosts a named day, the local martial scale behind the section.

luna: The source section stages charging horses as a force against a human crowd; this ayah commands preparation of war steeds to deter an enemy. It gives the horse's military force a defensive counterpart.
terra: Had the disrupters joined the army, they would have rushed through its midst seeking discord, a specific internal penetration of a gathered force.

luna: The source section says ج-م-ع names the gathering of people; here God gathers everyone and separates the idolaters from their claimed partners. It gives the mass gathering a concrete scene of separation. | terra: وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا is followed by a command separating associators from their partners, so the undifferentiated crowd becomes a scene of disclosure.

luna: The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; after 10:28 gathers everyone, this ayah says each soul is tested for what it did and returned to God, its true Lord. It supplies the individual's reckoning within the gathered scene.
terra: On the day God gathers them, earthly duration seems one hour and they recognize one another, making the former human crowd fleeting before the final meeting.
terra: Divine bounty and mercy are خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ, setting what people accumulate against the final divine collection.
terra: Noah challenges his people to collect their plan and partners before acting against him, applying gathering to a hostile coalition and its settled purpose.
terra: Even when people fold their breasts to hide, God knows what they conceal and disclose, setting the limit that 100:10's exposure completes.

luna: The source section says the root ج-م-ع names both the attacked human جمع and the great gathering day; this ayah calls it a day when people are gathered and witnessed (مشهود). It makes the local crowd open onto the universal assembly, where presence itself marks the day. | terra: The day is both مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النَّاسُ and مَشْهُودٌ, placing the section's crowd-root and presence/witness-root together in the universal assembly.

luna: The source section's final day brings a crowd before its Lord; here all people appear before God together (برزوا لله جميعا), and the weak and proud argue. It shows a public assembly where the group's hierarchy is exposed. | terra: وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا stages all people exposed before God, after which the weak confront those who had been great.
terra: When earth and heavens are changed, وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ supplies the exposed common presence of the final day.

luna: The source section expands a local crowd into a final gathering; this ayah says the Lord will gather all people, with wisdom and knowledge. It connects the assembly's scale to the Lord's knowledge of those assembled. | terra: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ names the section's Lord as the one who gathers them and closes with His wisdom and knowledge.

luna: The source section connects the gathering day with the witness-root ش-ه-د; this ayah says that on the day a witness is raised from every community. It shows the gathered multitude represented community by community. | terra: يَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا makes every community present through a witness on the day when denials are no longer admitted.

luna: The source section joins the جمع crowd to the witness-root ش-ه-د; this ayah says a witness is brought from every community and the Messenger is brought as witness over his people. It makes communal witnessing part of the assembly's judgment. | terra: The repeated scene raises فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا from among its own people and brings the Messenger as witness over his audience.

luna: The source section says the final day gathers people and exposes what is inside; this ayah says each soul comes pleading for itself and is repaid in full. It specifies the individual claim and recompense within the multitude.
terra: A powerful force جَاسُوا خِلَالَ الدِّيَارِ moves through the midst of dwellings, a close nonlexical counterpart to raiders penetrating a settled crowd.
terra: Each person's deed-record is fastened to them and brought out on Resurrection as an open book, making a hidden moral total present for the self-reading of 17:14.

luna: The source section says the witness-root ش-ه-د bears on a person's knowledge of his own conduct; this ayah tells each person to read the record, with himself sufficient as reckoner. It makes self-accounting a specific counterpart to the person's testimony. | terra: اقْرَأْ كِتَابَكَ makes the person sufficient as his own reckoner, a judicial form of witnessing against oneself after inner contents become manifest.

luna: The source section's horses charge into a human group; here Satan is told to rally people with his cavalry and infantry (بخيلك ورجلك). The link is the specific image of mounted force mobilized with people, though this is a metaphorical command rather than a raid.

luna: The source section moves from a collective crowd to the day everyone is gathered; this ayah says each people will be called with its leader. It adds the way the universal assembly is addressed in identifiable communities.
terra: Humanity and jinn are imagined assembling for one shared task yet remaining collectively unable, a bounded use of the largest creaturely crowd.
terra: The rejected are gathered يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ blind, mute, and deaf, a reversed bodily procession toward Hell.
terra: At the latter promise God brings the addressed people لَفِيفًا, a mixed gathered mass that anticipates the image's enlargement of a local people.

luna: The source section scales a raided local crowd up to the day all people assemble; this ayah says God gathers them and leaves none behind (فلم نغادر منهم أحدا). It specifies the gathering's total reach. | terra: After the landscape is stripped bare, وَحَشَرْنَاهُمْ فَلَمْ نُغَادِرْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدًا makes explicit that no one remains outside the gathered crowd.

luna: The source section's gathering day places humanity before its Lord; following 18:47's gathering of everyone, this ayah shows them presented before the Lord in rows (صفا). The row itself adds an ordered public assembly to the prior verse's completeness. | terra: The people gathered in 18:47 are عُرِضُوا عَلَى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا; this ayah supplies their ordered presence before the Lord after collection.

luna: The source section's gathering day brings people before their Lord; after 18:47 gathers everyone and 18:48 presents them in rows, this ayah places the record and says it leaves nothing small or great uncounted. It supplies the detailed account confronting the assembly. | terra: After the people are gathered and presented in 18:47-48, they find مَا عَمِلُوا حَاضِرًا; even their deeds are collected into presence.
terra: مَجْمَعَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ uses the root for a physical meeting-place, expanding the section's مَجْمَع from gathered people to two seas' confluence.
terra: مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا marks arrival at the place between the two seas, combining meeting-place with the section's developed relation between two sides.

luna: The source section links a surprised crowd to humanity's final gathering; here people first surge into one another, then the trumpet is blown and they are gathered (فجمعناهم جمعا). The verse stages the scale change the section describes. | terra: After people surge into one another, the trumpet sounds and God says فَجَمَعْنَاهُمْ جَمْعًا, exactly enlarging a confused crowd into the final collection.

luna: The source section explains the root ش-ه-د through a gathering place and the act of being present; this ayah warns of the disbelievers' share in the scene of a tremendous day (مشهد يوم عظيم). It makes the Day itself a place of public appearance.
terra: God swears by رَبِّكَ to gather humans and devils, then لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ around Hell, combining assembly with compulsory presence.

luna: The source section moves from one attacked crowd to the gathering day; here the God-fearing are gathered to the Merciful as an honored delegation (وفدا). This is a specific, favorable form of the same mass movement. | terra: The God-fearing are gathered to the Merciful وَفْدًا, an honored delegation that differentiates one procession within the universal muster.

luna: The source section's final assembly brings the small crowd to a universal day; this neighboring verse drives criminals to Hell thirsty (ونسوق المجرمين). It sets the gathered crowd's punitive destination against the honored delegation in 19:85. | terra: The guilty are driven to Hell وِرْدًا, reversing the honored delegation of 19:85 and dividing the one gathered humanity by destination.
terra: Everyone in heavens and earth comes to the Merciful as a servant, defining the common status of the persons counted in 19:94.
terra: God has comprehended and counted every one of them exactly, giving the universal multitude an exhaustive individual accounting before 19:95.

luna: The source section expands one crowd to humanity's final gathering; this ayah says every person comes to the Merciful individually (فردا). It marks the personal arrival within the universal day. | terra: Although God has counted them all, every one comes to Him individually on Resurrection, preserving individual exposure inside the universal gathering.
terra: The appointed public encounter is يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ when يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ ضُحًى, a worldly day defined by people being assembled at a set time.
terra: Pharaoh فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتَى collects his whole stratagem before coming to the appointed public encounter, extending gathering from people to a plan.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع names a human group and places horses amid it; this ayah tells the magicians to gather their plan and come in a row for their contest. It offers a specific, worldly gathering into formation before a confrontation. | terra: The magicians are told to collect their whole scheme and then come in one row, joining gathered intention to an ordered public company.

luna: The source section describes a great gathering after the trumpet; this ayah says the trumpet is blown and the criminals are gathered on that day, blue-eyed. It narrows the universal assembly to a marked group under judgment. | terra: The trumpet is blown and the guilty are gathered that day زُرْقًا, adding a marked bodily condition to the assembled crowd.
terra: On that day everyone follows the caller without deviation and voices fall quiet, giving the gathered sinners of 20:102 one direction and subdued collective sound.
terra: The one who turns from remembrance is gathered يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَعْمَى, defining an individual's altered place inside the universal assembly.
terra: رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمَى lets the gathered person address his Lord from within the condition announced in 20:124.

luna: The source section links the gathering day to the witness-root ش-ه-د; this ayah says God will judge among the several religious communities on Resurrection Day and is witness over all things. It brings communities and divine witness into the same judgment scene. | terra: After enumerating religious communities, the ayah says God separates them on Resurrection and is شَهِيدٌ over everything, joining assembled plurality and witness.
terra: The Messenger is شَهِيدًا over the community and they are شُهَدَاءَ over humanity, extending the witness relation of 2:143 without its middle-word.

luna: The source section's final gathering is the scale beyond a local human group; this ayah says God spread people through the earth and that they will be gathered to Him (تحشرون). It links dispersal across the world to assembly before God. | terra: The one who multiplied people across the earth is also the one وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, reversing earthly dispersal into one destination.

luna: The source section links a small crowd to the day everyone is gathered; this ayah says that when the trumpet is blown, family ties will not connect people and they will not ask one another. It sets a boundary on the tribal relations that make a local crowd a community. | terra: When the trumpet is blown, kinship no longer operates and people do not question one another, dissolving ordinary crowd-relations inside the final muster.
terra: وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذَابَهُمَا طَائِفَةٌ requires a group to be present at a punishment, joining witnessed attendance to an actual gathered public.

luna: The source section's root ش-ه-د concerns witnessing; this ayah says that on the Day their tongues, hands, and feet testify against people about what they did. It specifies how the gathered person's conduct becomes public testimony. | terra: On that day tongues, hands, and feet تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ, turning each person's own body into witnesses when concealed deeds are exposed.

luna: The source section lets the final day gather humanity; here God gathers those who worshipped and what they worshipped, then asks whether the worshippers misled them. The assembly becomes a confrontation between a group and its supposed leaders. | terra: God gathers the worshippers and what they worship, then questions the latter, turning assembly into exposure of who misled whom.
terra: Those gathered عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ form the worst-positioned procession, a judgmental reversal of the charging crowd.
terra: The same counsel orders city-gatherers to be dispatched, a repeated worldly use of commissioned agents who assemble a crowd for confrontation.
terra: فَجُمِعَ السَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقَاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ joins gathering, an appointed time, and a known day on the smaller human stage.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع names a human crowd; here Pharaoh's people are summoned to assemble (مجتمعون) for the public contest. This is a worldly crowd gathered to watch a confrontation, a smaller counterpart to the final assembly. | terra: The call هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُجْتَمِعُونَ supplies the public crowd whose appointed gathering is announced in 26:38.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع names a mass of people, and its local scene is a military incursion; this ayah says Pharaoh sends gatherers into the cities to assemble his force. It shows a ruler deliberately collecting a crowd for confrontation. | terra: Pharaoh sends musterers through the cities, initiating the collection of the pursuing force whose two crowds finally see each other in 26:61.
terra: Pharaoh's people describe themselves as a wholly alert company after the muster, characterizing the pursuing crowd before its sunrise advance.
terra: The mustered force pursues at sunrise, supplying both the morning movement and the approaching crowd immediately before the two hosts see one another.

luna: The source section's جَمْع image is a human crowd met by an approaching force; this ayah describes the two groups coming into sight of each other (تراءى الجمعان) as Moses' people face Pharaoh's force. It supplies a direct encounter between assembled crowds. | terra: When تَرَاءَى الْجَمْعَانِ, the two massed companies see one another, a direct battlefield use of the crowd-root before a decisive encounter.
terra: Solomon's forces of jinn, humans, and birds are mustered and held in ordered ranks, a concrete royal and military gathering on the smaller scale.
terra: The queen says she decides no affair until her counselors are present with her, a council scene using witnessing in the developed sense of attendance.
terra: Kings, إِذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً, ruin it and lower its honored people, spelling out the social reversal implicit when an armed force enters a settlement.
terra: On the day God gathers مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ فَوْجًا of deniers, each cohort is restrained, showing ordered subgroups within the greater muster.
terra: The trumpet terrifies everyone in heavens and earth except those God wills, and all come to Him humbled, combining universal summons with an explicit exception.
terra: God draws مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا and demands proof, showing how the collected peoples become an evidentiary gathering.
terra: Earlier generations stronger in force and أَكْثَرُ جَمْعًا show gathering as amassed worldly resources or followers, which do not prevent divine reckoning.
terra: The question whether God best knows what lies in all people's breasts makes inward content a universally known field rather than a private secret.

luna: The source section turns a human crowd toward the final gathering; this ayah says that on Resurrection Day people will disavow one another and curse the bonds they formed around idols. It shows a group's worldly attachments reversing at the day of account.
terra: When the Hour rises, يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ; the gathering day is also the moment the common crowd separates by outcome.
terra: Those who deny are فِي الْعَذَابِ مُحْضَرُونَ, using compulsory presence for the condemned outcome of resurrection.
terra: Attackers come from above and below while the besieged community is caught between them; the link to the section's middle-of-a-crowd raid is specific but nonlexical.
terra: God addresses the Prophet as a witness among his commissioned roles, identifying who bears testimony over the community brought to judgment.

luna: The source section lets the root ج-م-ع name a crowd and the day humanity is gathered; here the speaker says their Lord will gather them and judge between them in truth. It adds adjudication to the assembly.
terra: Those who strive against the signs are فِي الْعَذَابِ مُحْضَرُونَ, another use of being made present as an eschatological destination.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع names the assembly, and its witness-root ش-ه-د names presence; this ayah says that on the day God gathers everyone, He asks the angels whether these people worshipped them. It makes the gathering a scene of testimony and questioning. | terra: God gathers them all, يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا, then questions the angels, joining universal presence with testimony about earthly allegiance.

luna: The source section joins gathering with witnessing; answering God's question in 34:40, the angels deny being worshipped and declare God their protector. Their answer completes the prior verse's scene of the gathered being confronted with testimony.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع takes a human crowd toward the Last Day; this ayah says every one will be brought together before God (جميع لدينا محضرون). It stresses that no human stands outside the assembly. | terra: Every generation is جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ, joining the crowd-root with the section's developed sense of being present before God.
terra: A single cry seizes people while they are disputing, a death-summons that contrasts with the later single cry making everyone present before God.

luna: The source section turns from horses rushing into a small crowd to the resurrection gathering; here, after the trumpet, people stream from graves toward their Lord (ينسلون). Their urgent movement carries the raid's forward rush into the final assembly. | terra: The trumpet sends people streaming from graves toward رَبِّهِمْ, turning the surah's rushing movement into resurrection's mass advance toward their Lord.

luna: The source section's whole-surah context includes the graves being overturned before the day; after people stream from graves in 36:51, this ayah records their question about who raised them from their resting place and the answer that the Merciful's promise is true. It completes the emergence scene with recognition of the summons. | terra: Between the grave-rush of 36:51 and collective presence of 36:53, the awakened crowd recognizes that the messengers' promised resurrection was true.

luna: The source section says the great crowd is gathered on a day; here one cry is enough, and all are together and brought before God (جميع لدينا محضرون). It makes the universal gathering immediate and complete. | terra: One cry makes every person جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ; the ayah joins total gathering to being made present before God.
terra: Once all are present in 36:53, this ayah states the result: no soul is wronged and each is repaid only for what it did.

luna: The source section says the witness-root ش-ه-د is about being present; this ayah seals mouths on the Day and has hands speak while feet bear witness. It shows the body testifying in the accounting the gathering makes possible. | terra: الْيَوْمَ hands speak and feet تَشْهَدُ, making bodily testimony part of the same day on which everyone is collectively present.
terra: زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ is enough for everyone suddenly to be looking, directly paralleling the single sound that completes the gathering in the section.
terra: The people suddenly raised by the one cry recognize their woe and name what has overtaken them as the Day of Recompense.
terra: The answer identifies the crowd's recognized day as the Day of Decision they had denied, stating the purpose of their sudden collective presence.

luna: The source section scales a small crowd up to the final gathering; this ayah commands that the wrongdoers, their counterparts, and what they worshipped be gathered and led to Hell. It specifies a judgment assembly grouped by its participants and deeds. | terra: احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا commands the active collection of wrongdoers, their kinds, and their objects of worship for judgment.
terra: After the gathering command of 37:22, this ayah directs the collected company إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ, specifying its destination.
terra: وَقِفُوهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ مَسْئُولُونَ halts the gathered company in compulsory attendance for questioning.
terra: A speaker in Paradise says that without his Lord's favor he would have been مِنَ الْمُحْضَرِينَ, marking the boundary of compulsory presence in punishment.
terra: After Elijah's people reject him, فَإِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ promises their being brought into the judgmental presence.
terra: Those implicated in the claimed kinship with the jinn know they will be brought into compulsory presence, another eschatological use of attendance.

luna: The source section brings the human crowd toward a day of gathering before its Lord; this ayah says people will dispute before their Lord on Resurrection Day. It adds open argument to the assembly's reckoning. | terra: All disputants contend before their Lord on Resurrection, turning common presence with the Lord into an adjudicated confrontation.
terra: Two trumpet blasts distinguish collapse from assembly: after the second, فَإِذَا هُمْ قِيَامٌ يَنْظُرُونَ, setting a sequence beside the section's single cry.

luna: The source section's witness-root ش-ه-د and final gathering meet here: on that day the prophets and witnesses are brought, the record is set down, and judgment is made in truth. It specifies testimony and records within the assembled judgment. | terra: In the illuminated judgment scene, وَجِيءَ بِالنَّبِيِّينَ وَالشُّهَدَاءِ brings prophets and witnesses into the assembled presence before judgment.

luna: The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; after 39:69's public record and judgment, this ayah says every soul is repaid in full for what it did. It states the individual's outcome in that scene.

luna: The source section says the Day of Gathering joins many people but the day reveals loss and gain; here the disbelievers are driven to Hell in groups (زمرا). It shows the assembled multitude sorted into a condemned company. | terra: Those who disbelieved are driven to Hell زُمَرًا; the universal gathering resolves into condemned companies moving to one gate.

luna: The source section's gathering day reaches all people; here the reverent are led to the Garden in groups (زمرا). Paired with 39:71, this gives the assembly distinct and opposite destinations. | terra: Those who feared their Lord are driven to the Garden زُمَرًا, the answering procession and destination opposite 39:71.
terra: God sends the warning to announce يَوْمَ التَّلَاقِ, another name for the day defined by everyone meeting in one divine presence.

luna: The source section says what lies in the breasts is collected on the final day; this ayah describes people as exposed before God with nothing hidden from Him. It states the exposure of what had been concealed. | terra: On that Day of Meeting, هُمْ بَارِزُونَ and nothing about them is hidden from God, matching the collection of concealed contents.

luna: The source section joins hidden contents to the day of account; after 40:16 exposes everyone, this ayah says each soul is repaid for what it earned and no injustice is done. It completes the exposure with its consequence.
terra: God knows treacherous eyes and مَا تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ, naming precisely the hidden interior that the section says will be gathered out.

luna: The source section says the root ش-ه-د can name a gathering place and being present; this ayah names the day when the witnesses stand (يوم يقوم الأشهاد). It makes witnessing a public event of the final day.
terra: Enemies of God are gathered to the Fire and فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ, held in ordered ranks so none outruns the collective procession.

luna: The source section says what was hidden in breasts is collected; here, when people reach the Fire, their hearing, eyes, and skins testify against them. It shows concealed deeds becoming evidence at the end-time reckoning. | terra: When the gathered enemies reach the Fire, hearing, sight, and skins شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ about their deeds.

luna: The source section connects inner contents with testimony; after the body parts testify in 41:20, this ayah records the people asking their skins why they testified and the skins answering that God made them speak. It completes the prior verse's exposure scene. | terra: The condemned ask their skins لِمَ شَهِدْتُمْ عَلَيْنَا, exposing the unexpected witnesses within their own bodies.

luna: The source section names the great day with the root ج-م-ع; this ayah warns of يَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ, when people are assembled and divided between the Garden and the Blaze. It joins gathering to the fates that make the assembly consequential. | terra: يَوْمَ الْجَمْعِ is named explicitly, and the one assembly resolves into two companies, one in the Garden and one in the Blaze.

luna: The source section scales a crowd to the gathering of everyone; this ayah says God can gather the creatures He has dispersed through the heavens and earth whenever He wills (على جمعهم). It widens the image beyond a human encampment.
terra: وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ places human accumulation beneath the Lord's mercy, whose authority culminates in gathering them.

luna: The source section moves from a local human group to the final day; this ayah says that close friends become enemies to one another on that day, except the God-fearing. It marks how earthly group bonds can reverse when the assembly's true affiliations appear.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع names people collected for a day; this ayah calls the Day of Decision the appointed time for all together (أجمعين). It makes the day a common appointment for the whole multitude. | terra: يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ مِيقَاتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ makes the Day of Decision one appointment encompassing every member of the crowd.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع names the final gathering; this ayah moves from God's giving life and causing death to His gathering people for the Resurrection Day. It connects the grave's return to the day on which all are brought together. | terra: God gives life, causes death, then يَجْمَعُكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ, stating the whole movement into the assembly as one divine action.

luna: The source section moves from a local crowd to the final day; this ayah shows every community kneeling and each community summoned to its record. It makes the gathered mass legible as accountable communities. | terra: Every community is seen kneeling and تُدْعَى إِلَى كِتَابِهَا, so the universal crowd becomes distinct peoples summoned to their records.

luna: The source section says what lies in the breasts is collected for the day; after 45:28 summons each community to its record, this ayah says the record speaks the truth about what people did. The record supplies the evidence behind the assembly's accounting. | terra: The book speaks truth over the kneeling communities of 45:28 because their deeds were being copied, explaining what the assembly discloses.

luna: The source section cites 45:28's gathered communities called to their records; this next ayah says those who believed and did good are admitted by their Lord into mercy. It gives one destination of the assembled communities.

luna: The source section cites 45:28's universal summons to community records; this next ayah addresses the disbelievers and recalls that they acted arrogantly and were criminals. It gives the opposing outcome and the conduct it answers.

luna: The source section's ج-م-ع moves from a human group toward the final assembly; this ayah says that when people are gathered, the beings they invoked become their enemies and deny their worship. The assembly reverses the alliance that formed the group. | terra: When humanity is gathered, the beings they worshipped become their enemies and deny that worship, so the assembly exposes earthly relations.

luna: The source section says what lies in the breasts is collected; this ayah asks whether people with sickness in their hearts think God will not bring out their rancor (أضغانهم). It names a specific hidden content that becomes exposed. | terra: Those with disease in their hearts suppose God will not bring out أَضْغَانَهُمْ; the ayah directly promises disclosure of inward contents.
terra: The repeated commissioning sends the Prophet as witness, bearer of good news, and warner, connecting present proclamation to later testimony.
terra: God knows what the human self whispers and is nearer than the jugular vein, defining the prior divine knowledge of the contents later exposed.

luna: The source section's final gathering is linked to the trumpet; this ayah says the trumpet is blown and calls the moment the promised day. It gives the summons immediately preceding the individual procession in 50:21. | terra: The trumpet is blown and the ayah identifies this as the promised day, opening the sequence in which every soul arrives with driver and witness.

luna: The source section says the witness-root ش-ه-د involves presence at the gathering; following the trumpet in 50:20, this ayah says every soul comes with a driver and a witness (سائق وشهيد). It makes each person's presence and testimony explicit. | terra: Every soul comes with a driver and شَهِيدٌ, assigning individual witness and escort to each member of the universal crowd.

luna: The source section says what is hidden in the breasts is collected; after each soul arrives with a witness in 50:21, this ayah says the covering is removed and sight is sharp. It completes the arrival with the removal of concealment. | terra: The veil is removed and sight becomes sharp, describing the new exposure of the soul that has just arrived with its driver and witness.
terra: The command to listen for the caller from مَكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ introduces the common summons whose result 50:42 calls the day of emergence.
terra: All hear الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ, and the ayah identifies it as يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ, the sounding that brings the buried crowd out.

luna: The source section's local جمع opens toward all people gathered on the Last Day; this ayah describes the earth splitting and people rushing out, then calls that assembly an easy gathering for God (حشر علينا يسير). It supplies the grave-to-assembly scene. | terra: The earth splits from them as they emerge سِرَاعًا, and the ayah names the event حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ, a swift universal muster.
terra: A caller summons people to something dreadful; this is the initiating voice toward which the grave-crowd of 54:7-8 emerges and hurries.

luna: The source section moves from a crowd held together in the raid to the day of assembly; this ayah pictures people emerging from graves like scattered locusts (جراد منتشر). The dispersed swarm is a specific counter-image to the gathered crowd. | terra: They leave graves like جَرَادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ; the one gathered humanity appears visually dispersed like locusts while moving toward one summons.

luna: The source section's horses rush into a crowd, and its final scene gathers all people; following the scattered emergence in 54:7, this ayah says they hasten toward the caller. It completes the image of dispersed people moving together toward summons. | terra: مُهْطِعِينَ إِلَى الدَّاعِ gives the scattered multitude of 54:7 its common direction: all hurry toward the caller on the hard day.
terra: نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُنْتَصِرٌ voices the host's confidence immediately before 54:45 overturns it, sharpening the surprise carried by a crowd's defeat.
terra: سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ depicts a confident gathered host suddenly defeated and turning its back, closely matching the vulnerability of the raided crowd.
terra: مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ restages the physical meeting implicit in مَجْمَع البحرين without using the gathering-root.
terra: بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ places a boundary between the two meeting seas of 55:19, clarifying that meeting can preserve two sides.
terra: الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ defines the full temporal span of the crowd that 56:50 says will be gathered at one known appointment.
terra: لَمَجْمُوعُونَ إِلَى مِيقَاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ supplies the appointed day on which the former and latter named in 56:49 become one collected multitude.
terra: God يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا, reports their deeds, has counted what they forgot, and is شَهِيدٌ over all: gathering, accounting, and witness converge.

luna: The source section treats gathering as humanity brought together before God; this ayah tells people to fear God, to whom they will be gathered (تحشرون). In its context of private conversations, it makes that future assembly a boundary on present speech.

luna: The source section ties the final day to what is exposed about people; this ayah says God raises and gathers them all, where they swear to Him as they had sworn to people. It makes hidden duplicity visible in the universal gathering. | terra: On the day God raises them جَمِيعًا they swear to Him as they swore to people, while God remains witness over their false performance.
terra: The fortified people are struck from where they did not expect and terror enters their hearts, plausibly echoing the crowd's sudden capture in the raid.
terra: The opponents appear gathered together while their hearts are scattered, directly opposing an outward crowd to the divided contents that lie within breasts.

luna: The source section moves from a people gathered as a local community to the last day; this ayah says relatives and children will not benefit people on Resurrection Day, when God judges between them. It marks the limit of kinship as support in the final assembly.
terra: Fighters stand صَفًّا like a solid structure, a plausible ordered counterpart to cavalry breaking into the middle of an opposing gathered force.
terra: يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ is the recurring human gathering-day named by the same root, a weekly small-scale counterpart to the greatest Day of Gathering.
terra: After the Friday gathering-prayer, فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ sends the congregation outward, the ordinary cycle of gathering followed by dispersal.
terra: A congregation انْفَضُّوا toward trade and leaves the Messenger standing, opposing gathered presence with dispersal driven by worldly provision.

luna: The source section says what is in the breasts is collected and names 64:9 as the Day of Gathering; this ayah says God knows what people conceal and what they declare, and what is in breasts. It connects the gathering day in this surah with prior knowledge of the inner contents. | terra: In the surah that names the Day of Gathering at 64:9, God knows what people conceal, disclose, and what lies in breasts.

luna: The source section's root ج-م-ع moves from a human crowd to the Day of Gathering; this ayah says God gathers people for يَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ and calls it the Day of mutual gain and loss. That name brings the crowd's gathering into the reckoning of what each person has gained or lost. | terra: يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ gives the gathering its Quranic name and makes that assembly the day when true gain and loss appear.
terra: Concealed or public speech is equally known because God is عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ, matching the Lord's knowledge after inner contents are collected.

luna: The source section scales a human crowd up to the gathering day; this ayah says God spread people through the earth and that they will be gathered to Him (تحشرون). It joins worldwide dispersion to return before God. | terra: God who scattered humanity through the earth declares وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, compressing terrestrial multiplication back into a single destination.

luna: The source section's root و-س-ط places the horses between the crowd's two edges; this ayah calls one speaker أوسطهم among the garden owners, often read as their most balanced member. The link between a middle position and a voice within a group is plausible, though the sense is not spatial. | terra: أَوْسَطُهُمْ may mean the garden owners' most equitable or best member, plausibly extending the middle-root from spatial centrality to balanced judgment.
terra: A single blast on the trumpet begins this judgment sequence, another direct formulation of one sound initiating the final event.
terra: After the single trumpet blast and cosmic crushing, this ayah says that on that day the Event occurs, identifying the sounding's result.

luna: The source section says what lies in breasts is collected on the final day; this ayah says people will be exposed and no secret of theirs will remain hidden. It states the disclosure that the collection of inner contents implies. | terra: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَى مِنْكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ joins presentation before God to the disappearance of every hidden thing.

luna: The source section moves from a local crowd to the great gathering day; this ayah says no close friend will ask another about his state. It marks the failure of social bonds amid the day’s assembly.
terra: وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَى describes one who collects and stores away, opposing private accumulation to the day when persons and hidden contents are collected.

luna: The source section's first scene is horses racing into a crowd, later scaled to the final gathering; this ayah shows people rushing from graves as if racing to a marker. The image transfers the section's urgent motion from warhorses to resurrected people. | terra: People come from graves سِرَاعًا and rush as if toward a marker, closely recasting the surah's charging motion as mass resurrection.
terra: Humbled eyes and enveloping abasement identify the grave-rush of 70:43 as the very day the crowd had been promised.
terra: When God's servant stands calling Him, people nearly become لِبَدًا around him, a dense crowd arranged around a central figure.
terra: The Messenger is sent as a witness over the addressed people, giving the section's witness a communal speaker-addressee relation like Moses before Pharaoh.
terra: The trumpet is sounded, introducing the difficult day named in 74:9 and repeating the audible trigger of the gathering.
terra: The trumpet sounding of 74:8 is identified as a difficult day, giving the summons its temporal and judgmental character.

luna: The source section uses جَمْعًا for a crowd at the center of a raid; this ayah asks whether a human thinks God cannot collect his bones (نجمع عظامه) after death. It shifts collection from the whole crowd to the body's scattered parts. | terra: أَلَّنْ نَجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ applies the crowd-root to reassembling one person's bones, the bodily prerequisite of the universal gathering.

luna: The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for that day; this ayah says a person will be told what he sent ahead and left behind. It specifies what the day brings back into view. | terra: On that day the human is informed of what he sent ahead and left behind, an explicit disclosure of the completed contents of his life.
terra: بَلِ الْإِنْسَانُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ states the self-witnessing relation without the root, matching the human witness of 100:7 at disclosure.

luna: The source section's جمع joins a small people to the day all are gathered; this ayah calls the Day of Decision the day God gathers the present audience and earlier peoples (جمعناكم والأولين). It makes the assembly span generations. | terra: هَذَا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ جَمَعْنَاكُمْ وَالْأَوَّلِينَ combines the day, the present audience, and all earlier people in one judicial assembly.
terra: The Day of Decision is an appointed time, supplying the fixed communal appointment whose trumpet and arriving crowds appear in 78:18.

luna: The source section pictures a crowd at the center of a raid and then humanity gathering; this ayah says people will come on the appointed day in groups (أفواجا). It supplies a direct image of the final multitude arriving in bands. | terra: On the day the trumpet is blown, فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًا depicts humanity arriving as successive crowds rather than the few tents of the raid.

luna: The source section pictures people gathered on a great day; this ayah shows the Spirit and angels standing in rows, with speech permitted only by the Merciful. It adds an ordered assembly and its limit on speech.
terra: زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ supplies the single summons whose immediate result is the collective appearance described in 79:14.
terra: فَإِذَا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ shows the multitude suddenly present on the open surface after the single blast of 79:13.

luna: The source section turns a small attacked crowd into humanity assembled on the final day; this ayah says a person flees from his brother. It begins a specific reversal in which the local ties of a crowd no longer hold.

luna: The source section's local crowd is bound as a community; continuing the fleeing scene from 80:34, this ayah names a person's mother and father as those fled from. It extends the day-of-gathering reversal to the closest generational ties.

luna: The source section moves from a local people to the universal day; continuing 80:34-35, this ayah names the spouse and children from whom a person flees. It extends the reversal from parentage to one's household.

luna: The source section's gathering day brings everyone together; after 80:34-36 lists those a person flees, this ayah says each person has a concern that occupies him. It explains the individual urgency within the mass scene.
terra: At the cosmic judgment, عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَا أَحْضَرَتْ makes each soul know exactly what it has brought into presence.

luna: The source section's whole-surah context says graves are overturned before the day of collection; this ayah uses the same بعثر wording for when graves are scattered open. It supplies the grave-opening threshold to the gathering. | terra: When graves are overturned and emptied, the bodily containers release their contents immediately before each soul knows its moral contents in 82:5.
terra: After the graves are overturned, every soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind, paralleling the disclosure produced by collecting what breasts contain.

luna: The source section takes a human crowd toward a universal day of accounting; this ayah says no soul can avail another on that day and that command belongs to God. It marks the boundary between being gathered together and being able to help one another.

luna: The source section scales a small crowd into the gathering of all people; this ayah names the day mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds. It states the universal assembly as a scene of standing before God. | terra: The day is defined as the time when all people stand before the Lord of all worlds, a direct universal presence before their Lord.
terra: The record of the righteous يَشْهَدُهُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ, using witness in the sense of privileged presence around an unveiled record.

luna: The source section's whole-surah context asks what is in graves and hearts; this ayah says the earth casts out what is within it and empties itself. It pictures buried contents released before the final assembly.
terra: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ says God knows what they store within, tightly matching the section's collection of what breasts contain.
terra: الْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ supplies the eschatological day to which the witness and witnessed of 85:3 belong.

luna: The source section explains the root ش-ه-د as gathering and presence; this oath pairs a witness with that which is witnessed (شاهد ومشهود), near the promised day in 85:2. The link to public presence on a day is specific, though the oath's referents are interpreted in more than one way. | terra: شَاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ pairs witness and witnessed immediately after the promised day of 85:2, echoing the section's gathering-place sense of witnessing.

luna: The source section's ح-ص-ل root describes collecting a thing, and the section applies it to what is in the breasts; this ayah says that on that day secrets are exposed (تبلى السرائر). It gives a direct parallel for hidden contents brought into view. | terra: يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ makes the day specifically the testing and exposure of inner secrets, the closest thematic parallel to collecting what breasts contain.
luna: The source section's gathering day follows the overturning of graves; this ayah says the earth throws out its burdens. It gives the buried multitude's emergence a vivid counterpart.

luna: The source section expands from a raided crowd to a final gathering; this ayah shows people coming out in separate groups to be shown their deeds (أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم). It joins collective emergence to individual accounting. | terra: On that day people issue أَشْتَاتًا to be shown their deeds: the assembled humanity disperses into distinct parties for disclosure.

luna: The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; this ayah says whoever has done an atom's weight of good will see it. It gives one side of what the gathering's disclosure makes visible. | terra: The people dispersed to see their deeds in 99:6 each see even an atom's weight of good, specifying the disclosed contents of that day.

luna: The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; this ayah says whoever has done an atom's weight of evil will see it.
